sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's geothermal pipeline (PGEO, BRPT) benefits from state-mandated capacity targets and Baseload pricing, insulating it from global rate swings and making it a structural compounder.
Domestic solar demand is accelerating via rural electrification and industrial rooftop mandates, favoring local integrators (PKPK) over import-dependent US peers facing tariff and IRA uncertainty.
Climate-tech capital flows are bifurcating: US names (RUN, FSLR) trade on Fed policy, while ASEAN players gain from sovereign green funds and JETP disbursements, creating a persistent valuation gap.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian geothermal and solar names (PGEO, BRPT) on resilient domestic demand and tariff support; avoid US-exposed equipment makers (RUN, FSLR) where rate-cut repricing is fading. Position for Q3 earnings beats in IDX-listed utilities, and trim longs into any index-level bounce above 1% as global clean-energy sentiment stays fragile.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Ramadan and Lebaran demand cycles are the dominant near-term catalyst, driving restocking in poultry (AYAM, SGRO) and processed food (BOGA, PCAR) with a predictable 4-6 week lead time.
IDX consumer names are decoupling from US FMCG, as local currency stability and domestic purchasing power support premium valuations versus US-listed peers, sustaining a structural re-rating.
Small-cap consumer plays (AGAR, ERTX, JELI) show speculative spikes with thin liquidity, creating outsized alpha opportunities but requiring strict stop-losses due to high reversal risk.
sectors.ai: Buy selective consumer names with hard earnings proof, not beta. AGAR, ERTX, and JELI are momentum-driven but fragile; prefer BOGA and AYAM for volume-led recovery and margin resilience. Trim exposure to US-linked FMCG names as IDX outperformance widens. Rotate into poultry and processed-food plays ahead of Ramadan restocking, targeting 8-12% upside over 6 weeks.

Position for Q3 capex announcements and Jokowi legacy projects; trim any position that breaks its 20-day moving average.

Fuel subsidy rationalization and diesel price volatility favor operators with diversified fleets and fuel-efficient assets, penalizing laggards with older, fuel-heavy trucks.

Hold PORT for infrastructure-linked upside as port throughput data improves. Avoid chasing LOPI/TAMU; their moves are retail-driven and mean-revert within 48 hours.
